name: Per-member vote of the Asamblea Nacional on the Ley de Solidaridad (12 May 2016, 94 votes)
why: Would give each assembly member who voted for the one-off levy on net wealth; the Assembly publishes votes in its plenary records (Histórico de Actas del Pleno).
note: No per-member list is published for the vote of 12 May 2016 (the Assembly gives 94 of 127 present); searched in rounds 1, 2 and 4.

name: Informe de minoría / alternatives of the Revolución Ciudadana bloc on the VAT bill, January 2024
why: Bloc communiqué with a tax on fortunes above USD 1 million; the original text and the other members who signed it are not read.
note: Bloc position recorded from El Universo, El Mercurio (Manta), Primicias and Prensa Mercosur; the minority report itself was not found.

name: Frente Unitario de Trabajadores (FUT)
why: A 2020 column says the FUT proposed a permanent tax on large fortunes; a 2024 FUT list of ten alternatives was read without finding a wealth tax in it.
note: Its 2024 asks are on extraordinary profits and tax debts (exclusion X0006); no wealth-tax statement found in 3 searches.

name: Frente Popular
why: Named in the same 2020 column as a proposer of a permanent tax on large fortunes.
note: No statement of its own found.

name: Leonidas Iza
why: CONAIE president who presented the Parlamento Popular proposal of 31 October 2019 (taxes on the patrimonio of the economic groups); his own wording is not quoted in the source.
note: Three searches: no statement of his own on a wealth tax; the organisation rows stand.

name: Propuesta económica del Parlamento Popular / CONAIE, 31 October 2019
why: The original document would show whether the 5% on the patrimonio of economic groups was meant as a wealth tax and who drafted it.
note: Proposal recorded from the Primicias report (CONAIE rows); the document itself was not found.

name: Wilma Andrade
why: Vice-chair of the Comisión de Desarrollo Económico that reshaped the 2021 contribution on net wealth; her own position is not stated in the source.
note: Her quoted statement is that the committee left the contributions without consensus; no support shown.

name: Simón Cueva
why: Finance minister who defended the 2021 contribution on net wealth before the Assembly; no statement of his was read.
note: No statement of his on the contribution found in three searches.

name: Informe para primer debate, Comisión de Desarrollo Económico, 13 November 2021
why: The report lists its signatories (assembly members who backed the contribution on net wealth).
note: The Assembly notes give totals only, on whole reports.

name: Oxfam and Latin American tax-justice groups on Ecuador
why: Oxfam regional reports mention Ecuador; no Ecuador-specific proposal was found.
note: No Ecuador-specific Oxfam proposal found in three searches.

name: Verónica Iñiguez
why: RC assembly member who called the October 2026 softening of fines on undeclared foreign assets a shield for large fortunes; not a wealth-tax proposal yet.
note: Her remark concerns fines on undeclared assets, not a wealth tax.

name: Debate of the Ley de Apoyo Humanitario, May 2020: speakers who asked to tax large fortunes
why: The Assembly says several members agreed on taxing bank profits, large fortunes and companies in tax havens, without naming them.
note: The Assembly note does not name the speakers.
